To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the separation of palmitate and unsaturated fatty acids from palm fatty acid distillates in a counter-current column with supercritical carbon di-oxide as solvent can be performed successfully.
the separation of palmitoleic and oleic acids from PFAD can be performed in a single column with supercritical CO2 as solvent and that the use of a second column is not required.
it is feasible to design a continuous multistage countercurrent extraction process for the separation of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids in a supercritical carbon dioxide solvent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the separation of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids from palm fatty acid distillates using supercritical carbon dioxide.
the separation of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids from PFAD in a counter-current column with supercritical carbon-dioxide.
the development of an integrated process design method for the separation of multiconponent mixtures using supercritical carbon dioxide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
supercritical carbon dioxide extraction is a promising alternative to the classical solvent extraction process.

the separation of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids in continuous multistage counter-current columns with Supercritical Carbon Dioxide is a promising and feasible alternative to the conventional methods.

the process design methodology for the separation of multiconponent mixtures in continuous multistage countercurrent columns with supercritical CO2 as solvent is a very promising tool for the design of separation processes in the field of chemical engineering.

it was possible to separate palmitic acid from PFAD in a continuous countercurrent column with supercritical carbon dioxyde as solvent.

we developed a process design methodology which can be applied to any separation task in counter-current columns using supercritical carbon dioxide as solvent, and that we demonstrated the application of the methodology to the separation of saturated and unsaturated fatty acids from PFAD.

the separation of palmitate and oleate/linoleate in counter-current columns can be achieved at high purity and yields with low solvent consumption.
